blocks.text: AI infrastructure that arrives finished. This proposal is generated from configuration version a70260a2; every number in it comes from the same model that produces the drawings, bill of materials, digital twin and commissioning script.

Harbor Street Accounting needs 1 kW of IT capacity for a AI inference edge workload at Portland, ME. We propose one BEN 1: a 10-inch 8U desk / shelf mini rack (open or semi-enclosed) (DeskPi RackMate T1 (10-inch 8U) class) fitted out as a complete data center with 1 rack(s), Office air: filtered, sound-damped extraction path (no refrigerant) with N redundancy, a 1 x 1.0 kVA UPS giving 10 minutes of ride-through, clean-agent fire protection and the BEN Controls layer (sensors, firmware, digital twin, dashboard).

BEN 1 arrives assembled and burnt in by Schreiber AI. It needs a NEMA 5-15R on a dedicated 15 A, 120 V circuit (12 A continuous at 80 %), a network port and a room that can take 649 W (2,213 BTU/h) of heat; estimated noise 45.2 dBA at 1 m (target 50).

Price for the hardware + ben controls option: $19,746 capital ($32,910 per kW IT) plus $480 per year (BEN Controls licence). 9 % of the underlying cost is at confirmed vendor prices, 66 % at manufacturer list price and 25 % is engineering estimate; the price is firm at engineering release, when the configuration is frozen.

Order to in-service: about 3 weeks: Schreiber AI assembles BEN 1 from stock kits, burns it in, ships it and sets it up (compute bought by us can add its own lead time, see section 7). No permits are needed for a plug-in unit; risks are disclosed in section 10.

blocks.text: These are the risks that apply to the ai inference edge profile, from the product risk register (docs/RISK_REGISTER.md, web/assets/risks.json). Each line says what the design covers and what remains the customer's decision or duty. Please read them before accepting the price.

rows: The grid fails for seconds to days. IT shuts down when the battery runs out and cooling stops at once unless it is on UPS or generator.
UPS ride-through (default 10 min), generator option with ATS, measured cooling ride-through (test E5), N+1/2N per profile.
Whether to buy the generator and fuel, the utility contract, and whether cooling is put on UPS.
Cooling stops when power is lost
If cooling is not on UPS, inlet temperature in a small container rises several degrees per minute at full load.
Ride-through measured in test E5 and published; option to put fans and pumps on UPS; generator start in 10 s; load-shed hooks.
Choose: accept a few minutes, add cooling to UPS, or add a generator.
Permit delay or unexpected AHJ requirement
The local authority may classify the container as a building, ask for a field evaluation or more fire protection, and take longer than the build.
Pre-application package, code summary, field-evaluation budget line, site requirements signed before build, parallel permit path in the schedule.
Pulling permits (or authorising us), zoning, neighbour relations.
UPS, switchgear, cooling units and transformers can take months and slip.
Long-lead orders at engineering release, approved alternates, stocked controls hardware.
Early deposit and configuration freeze; no late changes.
A new 12.47 kV service with primary metering and two pad-mount transformers is utility work on the utility's schedule, typically 26 to 52 weeks.
Interconnection application filed at order, utility window carried on the critical path, load letter and single-line ready at kick-off, temporary 480 V service for commissioning where allowed.
The utility contract and fees, land for utility equipment, easements.
The hall is a building (IBC Group B or F-1), not an equipment enclosure: plan review, state modular approval and inspections take 8 to 16 weeks before civil works can start.
Stamped permit set from the engineering release, state modular label on each module, pre-application meeting, civil package starts after permit, both occupancy classifications budgeted.
Zoning, land use, easements, neighbour notice, permit fees.

Every watt the AI box uses becomes heat in the room: a full cab12 is about 5,600 BTU/h, like a small space heater running all day. A closed closet with no air path heats up within hours and the AI box slows down or shuts off.

Heat-to-room figure on the quote and the data plate, site check before shipping (room cooling or a vent path sized for the unit), BEN Pod intake-temperature alarm before the IT throttles, heat to room measured at handover (E22).
Keep the vent path or door grille open, do not block the intake, tell us if the room changes.
Long lead times for large electrical gear (dense tiers)
1,600 to 2,000 A switchboards, large UPS frames, row CDUs and megawatt-class dry coolers have the longest lead times in the catalog, stretched by AI demand.
Long-lead orders at engineering release, frame agreements and reserved slots, approved alternates, long-lead items and dates named in the quote.
Early deposit and early configuration freeze.
A fault while a panel is open or a component failure can injure someone and damage equipment.
Arc-flash study and labels, selective coordination, listed dead-front gear, lockout points, NFPA 70E training at turnover.
Only qualified electricians work on it and the labels are followed.
Hot days, a failed cooling unit or more load than planned push inlet temperatures up; IT throttles or trips.
N+1 cooling, climate derate built into sizing, inlet sensors at three heights per rack with ASHRAE alarms, load-step and failover tests.
Keep IT load inside the configured kW, keep filters and coils clean, do not block containment.
A cable, battery or power supply fire would mean loss of IT, an agent discharge and downtime.
Very-early smoke detection, clean agent with 10-minute hold, HVAC shutdown, EPO, non-combustible liner, battery separation.
Fire marshal relationship, agent recharge contract, no combustible storage inside, insurance.
Roof, door seals, condensate or a liquid-cooling loop can leak and damage IT.
Rope leak sensors, condensate float alarm, drip trays, CDU auto pump stop on leak, propylene glycol only, seal inspection schedule.
Keep drains clear, respond to alarms, pad drainage.
A drifted sensor can make the dashboard look fine while the room is not.
Redundant sensors, idle cross-check (test E1), drift detection, 12-month or trigger-based recalibration.
Allow calibration visits, do not move sensors.
Dry coolers and condensers can exceed night-time limits at the property line.
Sound prediction at quote, low-noise fans and night setback, acoustic survey at SAT (test E10), barrier option.
Civil works, permits and utility connection can cost more than the allowance.
Firm box price after engineering release; site works quoted after survey; utility costs identified at survey.
Utility fees, civil works, permits, taxes, and changes after freeze.
Cooling energy rises in hot climates and with high utilisation.
Honest PUE estimate from the configuration, measured at SAT (test E9), economizer and variable-speed fans.
Hot-day make-up water is 2 to 8 cubic metres a day per 1,000 kW; drought rules or a weak supply can force the coolers to run dry and lose capacity on the hottest days.
Dry mode below 28 C, chilled-water option for hot climates, water quantity and drain confirmed at site survey, storage tank option, water management plan per ASHRAE 188.
Water supply contract, drought-rule compliance, sewer discharge permit for bleed water.
The three hall modules are sealed on site; the seams are the one part of the IP66 envelope not finished in the factory.
Factory compression gaskets and field EPDM cover strips with a drained cavity, joint seal hose test E15 at SAT and after any relocation, leak rope under each joint, semi-annual seal inspection.
Keep the roof clear of debris and snow beyond design, respond to alarms.
CDU pump failure on a high-density liquid loop
At 100–250 kW per rack the cold plates have seconds of margin, not minutes.
Pumps N+1 per row CDU with automatic failover, monthly proof, commissioning step 6 and experiment E18; low-flow critical alarm.
Choosing N+1 CDUs where the load justifies it.
A cab12 at full load uses most of a 20 A circuit. A heater, printer or coffee machine on the same circuit trips the breaker; the UPS carries the IT for a few minutes and then shuts it down.
Dedicated circuit required (15 A rack10, 20 A cab12), load limited to 80 % of the circuit in the configuration, clean shutdown on UPS input loss, input current measured at handover (E22).
Have the dedicated circuit installed and keep other loads and power strips off it.
A mini rack is small enough to carry and it holds your data.
Lockable cabinet (cab12) or cable-lock point (rack10), disk encryption on by default with the key held off the box, door-contact alarm through the BEN Pod, remote wipe of controller credentials.
Keep it in a lockable room, keep the recovery key safe, insure the equipment.
Someone adds a gaming PC, a cheap switch or an unlisted power strip because it fits. The unit runs hotter, louder and less reliably and may hold a part nobody can support.
Shipped full and labelled, additions by change order with a fit, heat and power check, only UL 62368-1 listed parts on the BEN 1 catalog, BEN Care flags unknown devices.
Ask before adding equipment; no extra power strips.
Small sites often have a backup job that has silently stopped. When a disk fails or ransomware hits, the restore does not work.
Backup to a second target set up at handover, BEN Care reports every failed backup, quarterly restore test on the maintenance list and checked remotely.
Keep the second backup target and do the quarterly restore test (or let BEN Care do it).
Lithium UPS batteries last about 3 to 5 years. An old battery holds the IT for seconds, so a short power blip becomes a hard shutdown.
Quarterly UPS self-test reported by BEN Care, battery-health alarm, replacement pack shipped before end of life with a prepaid recycling return, runtime measured at handover (E23).
Swap the battery when it arrives (about 10 minutes) or book the visit.
One rack is a large share of the unit (dense tiers)
On BEN 300 a single 132 to 155 kW liquid rack can be half or all of the IT. A fault in that rack, its manifold branch or its tap-off takes most of the unit's capacity with it.
Per-rack isolation valves and tap-off breakers, N+1 CDUs and pumps, failure domain (kW lost per single fault) printed in the proposal, BEN 1000 spreads load over more racks.
Decide whether the workload tolerates one failure domain or needs two units.
CDU or pump failure at full liquid load (dense tiers)
Liquid is the default on BEN 300 and BEN 1000, so a CDU or pump failure applies to every unit. Cold plates at 130 to 250 kW per rack have seconds of margin.
N+1 CDUs as the default, automatic failover, monthly proof of redundancy (BEN Care), test E18 at FAT and SAT, CDUs and pumps on UPS.
Keep the BEN Care proof running or do the monthly failover test.
Warm-water loops grow biofilm and scale faster; filters clog and cold plates lose margin over months.
Coolant to the OCP water-based spec or PG25, side-stream filtration, quarterly coolant sampling and filter changes on pressure drop, loop flow and temperature trended by the twin (E20).
Water analysis contract if not under BEN Care; never top up with tap water.
Weight on the 20 ft floor (dense tiers)
A current liquid AI rack weighs about 1.4 to 1.6 t. Two of them plus CDUs, UPS and batteries load a 20 ft frame close to its rating, and rack feet exceed what a container floor is built for.
Steel sub-floor spreading the load, PE structural check for the selected racks, racks set in at site when gross mass would exceed the frame rating, weighed at transport prep.
Crane and site access for setting racks in at site where needed.
Site fault current differs from assumption
Until the utility gives its fault current and voltage, arc-flash labels and some ratings are provisional.
Labels marked provisional until SAT; study updated with utility data; panel SCCR at least 65 kA.
Provide utility fault current and voltage before the unit ships.
A bad lift or rough transport can twist the frame or crack a weld.
Corner-casting lifts with spreader, PE-checked frame, shock loggers, set-down inspection, freight insurance; BEN 2000 modules lifted on engineered lugs with a 100 t crane and a certified lift plan.
Crane access, competent rigger, route survey for the high-cube height.
GWP limits and flammable-refrigerant rules are changing; a unit model can become unavailable for new installs.
Non-flammable refrigerant under 700 GWP chosen now, or water loops; EPA 608 technicians; small charges.
A specified part may be discontinued or lose its listing before or after build.
Approved alternates in the BOM, configuration freeze per unit, FAT repeats affected tests.
Person inside during agent discharge or refrigerant leak
Clean agent or a refrigerant leak can disorient or expose a technician inside.
Pre-discharge alarm with delay, abort switch, door interlock, refrigerant detector, purge ventilation, written entry procedure, non-flammable refrigerants.
Follow the entry procedure, keep training current.
Fans speed up when the AI box works hard, which can annoy a small office and lead to the unit being moved somewhere worse.
Sound-damped cabinet (cab12), low-speed fans, target 45 dBA or less at 1 m at full load, measured at handover (E21).
Place it away from desks where possible and keep the cabinet door closed.
